feedback_text: I need evening classes because my work schedule changes every week.
The campus is too far from my office, so a hybrid option would make the program possible.
I would choose the program that lets me study on weekends without interrupting work.
Shorter sessions and recorded lectures would help me keep up during busy periods.
Convenient scheduling matters more to me than rankings.
I want a program I can complete without taking a long leave from my job.
A flexible timetable would remove the biggest barrier to enrolling.
Online access is important because I travel frequently for work.
Tuition is the first thing I compare because I am paying without company support.
I need a clear return on investment before committing to the program.
Scholarships and installment payments would strongly affect my decision.
I want the most affordable credible degree, not extra facilities I will not use.
Total cost matters more than the advertised tuition fee.
I would pay more only if the career outcomes are clearly better.
The program must fit my budget and help me move into a higher-paying role.
Employer sponsorship would make me much more likely to enroll.
The school's reputation is important because I want the qualification to be recognized internationally.
I am looking for a prestigious program that signals leadership potential.
Rankings matter because they help employers compare programs quickly.
I want a degree from a school with a strong brand in Asia.
The alumni network and school reputation would support my transition into consulting.
I care about selective admissions because the cohort quality affects the value of the degree.
A respected degree would give me more credibility with senior clients.
The program should be known for producing capable general managers.
I want electives that match the technology sector rather than a generic curriculum.
The course should let me apply assignments to problems in my own company.
I need deeper training in analytics and strategy, not a broad review of business topics.
The ability to customize courses around my career goals is essential.
I value practical projects where faculty help us work through real decisions.
The curriculum should connect marketing, data, and product management.
I want rigorous classes that challenge how I currently make decisions.
Industry-specific examples would make the learning much more useful.
I want classmates from different industries who can broaden my perspective.
Access to experienced alumni is one of the main reasons I would join.
Small-group projects are valuable because I learn from how other managers solve problems.
I am looking for a community that continues after graduation.
The quality of the cohort matters as much as the quality of the faculty.
I want regular opportunities to meet founders and senior executives.
A collaborative culture would make the experience more valuable than independent study.
I would choose a program that actively connects students to employers and alumni.
